useFor: Pictures whose size the app does not control: framed whole or cropped without the page jumping, a gallery of attachments, a link unfurled, and one picture opened large.

combineWith.how: The skeleton reads the same --media-ratio as the frame it stands in for, so the picture replaces it without a jump.
The lightbox is a dialog opened with showModal() or ShowModalAsync, so the focus trap, Escape and the inert page are the platform's.
A folder of pictures is file tiles, whose thumbnails take the same transparency modifier as a frame.
Several pictures in one message are a .gallery--tight in a media bubble, each opening the lightbox.

notFor.text: Long text from a source the app did not author
A folder of files the reader selects and acts on
Slides the reader moves through one at a time
A PDF read in the page
A video with its title and transcript

useFor: A row of slides the reader may move through one at a time and is fine to miss: what a release brings, records worth a look.

combineWith.how: The dots are the deck's .deck-dot buttons, each with data-carousel-to naming its slide.
Each slide is a card of its own, side by side with --carousel-per-view and a peek at the next.

notFor.text: Content every reader needs
A sequence that has to be finished
Pictures the reader looks through and opens

useFor: A folder as a table or a grid of tiles, the files attached to a record, and uploads on their way up with their progress.

combineWith.how: A folder is a table in a card whose name column is a .file-cell, folders first, sorted and selected as any table is.
The path above the folder is a .breadcrumb, so the reader always knows which folder this is.
The dropzone above, and one .file-item per file under it while it uploads.
A .progress in .file-item-main is an upload under way, with how far it has got in the size column.
The count of selected tiles and the actions on them sit in a toolbar above the grid.
An empty folder says so where the table or grid would be, with the path still above it.

notFor.text: Choosing a file in a form
Pictures looked at rather than managed
Reading a PDF without downloading it

useFor: A video in the platform's own player, with its title, its length, its actions and a transcript to read, and a library of videos as tiles.

combineWith.how: A library of videos is a .file-grid--wide whose tiles carry .file-tile-play and their length.
The player reads --media-ratio, 16:9 unless it says otherwise, so the page does not jump when the metadata arrives.

notFor.text: Sound with no picture
A still picture opened large

useFor: A recording the reader plays: a call or a voicemail in the native player, a voice message as a waveform, and a track list.

combineWith.how: A voicemail or a playlist is a list whose rows play, the one playing marked aria-current.
A voice message in a thread is the same .audio-wave inside the bubble.
The player is the same .media-player as a video's, with no picture and a .media-transcript under it.
The player of the track playing sits under a card head as .media-player--flush, over the track list.

notFor.text: A live voice moving with the microphone
A recording with pictures

useFor: Long text the app did not author, set on the tokens and contained however wide it is, words changed between two versions, and a value withheld from the reader.

combineWith.how: Prose sits in a card body, with --prose-measure: none on the box and the class on an inner wrapper where the prose is the panel.
The same ins and del marks inside a line of a diff show the words that changed in it.

notFor.text: Rendered Markdown
Two versions of a text line by line
Formatted text the reader writes

useFor: Rendered Markdown wherever it appears, and a Markdown field the reader writes in with a toolbar and a live preview.

combineWith.how: The Write and Preview switch over the editor is a segmented control whose radios carry data-md-tab.
As a form field the textarea takes the label and hint, and the form's actions row follows it.
A picker of the app's own, awaited with ShowModalAsync, returns the text InsertMarkdownAsync puts at the caret.
A .markdown-body inside a bubble is how an assistant's answer reads as a message.

notFor.text: HTML that did not come from Markdown
Formatted text for readers who do not write Markdown

useFor: Two versions of a text line by line, unified or side by side, from a diff the app computes.

combineWith.how: The .diff-head names the file and counts the lines added and removed in go and danger badges.
Inside a changed line, ins and del mark the words that changed.
A diff straight in a card, under a head that names the file, takes .diff--flush, so the card draws the only frame.

notFor.text: A few words changed in running text
Code shown once, with nothing to compare

useFor: A block of code or output the reader copies: one file, several files as tabs in a card, or a long one clamped until opened.

combineWith.how: Several files in a card with tabs, one .code-block--flush per panel.
A block inside a card's body, or flush to its edges as the card's only content.
The command an agent ran, and its output, as blocks under the step.

notFor.text: A log that keeps growing
Two versions of a text compared
A value the reader copies from a field

useFor: A PDF read in the page through the browser's own viewer, with a bar to open or download it and a fallback where there is no viewer.

combineWith.how: The fallback inside the object is an empty state naming the document, with a link that downloads it.
A PDF opened from a gallery is a .lightbox-frame in the lightbox's stage.
A PDF in a card takes .pdf-frame--flush, with its name and actions in the card head instead of a bar.

notFor.text: A list of documents to download
A picture of a scanned page

useFor: Text or an address as a QR code a camera reads, with the text written beside it for the reader who cannot scan.

combineWith.how: A pairing code sits in a card body with the step that uses it above it and a button that copies the link under it, for the reader without a camera.

notFor.text: An address the reader clicks

useFor: Formatted text the reader writes — a note, a description, a reply — posted as HTML from a textarea, with the formats its toolbar offers and no others.

combineWith.how: The editor takes a .form-field's place with its label and hint, and the hidden textarea posts, resets and is required like any other field.
The slash menu is a .menu.editor-slash written inside the editor, one item per kind of block.
The notice for a pasted file it did not take is coloured by .form-warning at the editor's foot.
An image picker of the app's own, opened by cancelling sedna-editor-media and answered with InsertImageAsync.

notFor.text: Text written in Markdown syntax
Plain text with no formatting
A message in a conversation

useFor: A conversation between people: bubbles, groups and channels, replies and reactions, the composer, and the launcher that keeps it one tap away.

combineWith.how: Each message's avatar, and a group in the list of conversations as an .avatar-pair.
The emoji picker behind a reaction's add button is a popover holding .chat-emoji buttons.
A message's further actions, the destructive one a .menu-item--danger.
A file in a bubble is the same .file-item every file list uses.
The history arriving is skeletons in the thread's own shapes, mine on the end.
The conversations are a list of rows that navigate, each with its last line and an unread badge.

notFor.text: An agent's answer with reasoning, steps and sources
What happened to a record, in order
Messages the reader comes back to later
